method: Repository inventory textual review, not an occupational ontology or primary-source confirmation. All merges, splits, naming corrections and credential interpretations remain proposed/unresolved.

candidateGroups.reason: Reversed paired labels. Compare credentialed dietitian and nutritionist meanings before choosing article boundaries.
Therapy versus Therapist wording differs. Verify intended role before linking both appearances to one profile.
Similar laboratory technician labels require occupation and credential comparison; do not merge with Medical Laboratory Scientist by title alone.
One title names a technician; the other groups technician and technologist. Resolve scope and credential distinctions.
Titles mix broad imaging roles, specialties and credential abbreviations. Verify each against issuer descriptions; preserve each source appearance even when a profile covers a specialty.
Information and records labels may describe overlapping roles or a service rather than separate occupations. Verify scope and retain the service label unresolved.
Account titles may overlap while manager and technician levels differ; compare actual responsibilities and education.
Similar data job-family labels are not sufficient evidence of equivalence; compare research versus operational settings and role levels.
Closely related wording requires role-definition evidence before consolidation.
Associate, scientist and specialist may indicate different levels or duties; no automatic merge.
Compare monitor and research associate terminology and distinguish site coordination; no automatic merge.
Clinical pharmacology, pharmaceutical science and pharmacology labels overlap but may imply different training and settings.
Compare navigation and advocacy functions and employment settings rather than assuming synonyms.
Related counselor labels require scope and credential evidence; retain distinct source appearances.
Broad physician label may include surgical practice; do not delete the surgeon appearance or count a specialty as an independently established occupation without an explicit editorial decision.
